subject: National Value Education

questions.q: In basic civic terms, who is a **Citizen**?
options: Any individual who simply visits a country for a brief tourist vacation
A person who has a legal and recognized right to belong to a particular country
A foreign diplomat assigned to an embassy
Anyone who crosses an international border illegally
questions.explain: A **citizen** is a legally recognized member of a state or country, possessing full constitutional rights and owing allegiance to that country.
questions.exam: BECE National Values Education: Civic Education
questions.subject: National Value Education

questions.q: A child is born in Lagos to parents who are both recognized citizens of Nigeria. Which type of citizenship has this child legally acquired?
options: Citizenship by Naturalization
Citizenship by Registration
Citizenship by Birth
Citizenship by Conferment
questions.explain: When an individual acquires their citizenship status because they were born to parents who are citizens of that country, it is called **Citizenship by Birth**.
questions.exam: BECE National Values Education: Civic Education
questions.subject: National Value Education

questions.q: A foreign woman from Brazil marries a Nigerian man and decides she wants to become a Nigerian citizen. Which specific constitutional process applies to her situation?
options: Citizenship by Birth
Citizenship by Registration
Citizenship by Force
Citizenship by Inheritance
questions.explain: Under the constitution, a foreign woman married to a Nigerian man can acquire citizenship through **Registration**.
questions.exam: BECE National Values Education: Civic Education
questions.subject: National Value Education

questions.q: Which of the following best describes the process of acquiring citizenship by **Naturalization**?
options: A foreigner who has continuously lived in a country for a constitutionally specified long period and has shown good character applies to the government for citizenship
A person randomly discovering they have a Nigerian grandfather
A foreign tourist purchasing land in the capital city
A citizen of one country being captured as a prisoner of war by another country
questions.explain: **Naturalization** requires a foreigner to reside in the country for a statutory number of years, integrate into the society, possess good character, and officially apply for citizenship.
questions.exam: BECE National Values Education: Civic Education
questions.subject: National Value Education

questions.q: The process of becoming a citizen involves strictly following constitutional guidelines. Who holds the supreme power to grant citizenship by naturalization in Nigeria?
options: The State Governor
The Local Government Chairman
The President of the Federation
The Inspector General of Police
questions.explain: According to the Nigerian constitution, the power to approve and grant citizenship by naturalization or registration officially lies with the **President of the Federation**.
questions.exam: BECE National Values Education: Civic Education
questions.subject: National Value Education

questions.q: A foreigner who wishes to legally acquire Nigerian citizenship through **Naturalization** must satisfy several stringent constitutional conditions. Which of the following is typically a primary requirement?
options: Having actively served in the Nigerian military for one month
Being married to a Nigerian politician for exactly one week
Having lived in Nigeria continuously for a statutory period (e.g., 15 years) and being of good character
Donating a massive sum of foreign currency to the central government
questions.explain: To qualify for **Citizenship by Naturalization**, an alien must demonstrate integration by residing continuously in the country for a long statutory period (15 years in Nigeria), showing good character, and proving they can contribute to national progress.
